lead: leaving was never on the table, which is why the questions go all the way down. someone who might walk out is careful with the floor. the promise stands whatever comes up, so nothing under it is protected.
sun: the account a marriage runs on was the first thing you took apart — the reason given for the move, whose work actually got paid for, what the year of the illness settled between you. none of it held. underneath sits the arrangement neither of you would have signed if it had been read out on the day, and nothing since has moved it. you were looking for the bottom.
moon: and then you stay. a vow entered on purpose has no door built into it — no version of you drafting an exit while the finding comes up, no bad month ending with a suitcase in the hall. so the true account of a marriage gets made by the person obliged to be at that table for breakfast every morning for thirty more years, holding it.
pull: you took the ground out from under a promise you will keep anyway. nobody is leaving. the two of you go on living in the house, correctly, on nothing.
tension: from outside this is the durable one, the pair held up at other people's weddings. the reading indoors is colder. she has told you that nothing in her own history is allowed to stay a memory, that a story she liked telling got checked and came back wrong, and that the checking served no purpose she could see. she is right about the purpose. there was never one to serve.
cost: very few couples ever learn what they actually agreed to; yours has it, dated, with the flattering parts gone and every clause standing up. the promise obliges exactly what it obliged on the day. so the obligation now runs to a woman you can describe more accurately than she can bear being described, and thirty years is a long time at close range.

lead: your standing rests on a date anybody can look up. you outlasted the people who taught you, and now the questions are going under the method they taught, with nobody left above you to call it far enough.
sun: what everyone in the field was taught has a reason under it, and the reason has an afternoon under that — three people in a room settling a question of convenience nobody has reopened since. the descent through it is ordinary work for you, and it lands on a decision made by hand, for scheduling reasons, by people who never expected it to be carrying a discipline forty years later. duration proves nothing.
moon: the seniority is not an argument, and it functions as one. the date beside your name certifies that you outlasted, nothing more, but a finding from that seat arrives already settled, so what you bring up never gets the hostile reading it needs to be worth anything. and the layers below the paper survive in one memory now. it is yours. no one is left who can countersign it.
pull: you are the last person who was in the room and the first name on the register. the finding is right, and there is nobody alive who could usefully disagree with it.
tension: juniors do not argue with you, which is the difficulty rather than the compensation. someone eleven years in listens to you take the standard apart, agrees on the spot, and leaves with a conclusion he has not tested — the route a wrong one would travel just as easily. the ones your own age call it self-demolition and stop returning calls, and theirs was the only standing that could ever have slowed you down.
cost: a field's founding assumption gets checked once, if at all, and it happened here, from the one seat with the access and the memory. what comes back is accepted on the date beside your name rather than on the reasoning, so the reasoning has gone thirty years without a hostile reading. you can no longer separate the findings that would survive one from the ones that were deferred to.

lead: the answer arrived in the first week and you are six years in. every other chart has something that gets bored, or satisfied, or frightened of what comes up next. yours has the same instrument again where that would be.
sun: people bring you the thing nobody can explain, and they are right to. what nobody is ready for is that the explanation does not end the visit. the file stays open after the room has moved on, a matter closed to everyone's satisfaction eighteen months ago gets taken up again, and the second finding is worse than the first and equally sound. the room learns to phrase requests carefully and it changes nothing.
moon: the descent feeds on its own product. every floor removed puts the next one in view, and the view is what starts the next removal, so the work supplies its own reason to continue and nothing issues a competing one. there is no counterweight in the machinery — no part that tires of a subject, no part that wants a thing left standing more than it wants the cause.
pull: everything you have ever gone into is still open. the finding was not the end of it. it was the floor you were standing on when you saw the next one.
tension: the request is always narrow. look at the accounts, listen to the noise the engine makes, tell me whether the story about my father could be true. the narrow thing gets answered inside a week and the work carries on for a year, and people find they have no sentence available that closes it. they can ask you to stop. the asking costs them nothing and buys them nothing, and by then the ground they wanted checked is already up.
cost: hand this a failure that has defeated three sets of competent people and it comes back with the mechanism, sourced, from a depth nobody else would go to. the same motion has been running on your own account of yourself since you were young, undiluted, so nothing in there has gone unlifted. people who take a floor up have somewhere else to stand while they do it.

lead: you are on the coach at six with everyone else. the thing they are travelling for went to the bottom under you two winters back and did not hold, and nobody in the seats behind knows it.
sun: what people came for and what has actually been holding the room up are two different things, and you established that alone, over years, from the inside. under the stated reason sits an arrangement about who is owed deference, made early, by people whose names are on nothing. it is correct and it is not sayable. no size of it exists that could be handed to someone carrying a hymn book onto a bus.
moon: you keep the rhythm exactly. at the meeting, driving the van, one of the ones the newer arrivals are told to ask — and while that goes on you are sorting which parts of the shared account are carrying weight and which are decoration. the sorting never stops and never gets tabled anywhere. you belong to that body at full attendance and are nowhere inside it.
pull: you go where they go, at their speed, twenty years running. the thing they are all standing on came apart in your hands one winter and you have not mentioned it since.
tension: they ask you to take the newer ones, because turning up is the only evidence a congregation collects and you have twenty years of it. the small doubts come to you and you answer them honestly, which keeps people in. the honest answer to what they were asking sits three levels under where the question was pitched, and would take a few hundred people's footing with it. the ones who call you steadfast are describing something else.
cost: put you inside any body of people and within a season you can say which of its reasons are load-bearing and which are furniture. what you no longer have is the part of belonging that runs on not knowing. you arrive with them, you leave with them, and the hour they are all having together is the one thing in that room unavailable to you.
